metadata.proof: POST /api/inspections requires property_admin/property_manager but only validates inspector.role in {property_manager, maintenance_worker} via payload.inspector_id. No cross-property scope check. A manager can assign an inspector from another property to an inspection at their property. The inspector then gains access via ensure_inspection_scope's inspector_id == user.id path, leaking inspection data across tenants.

extra.message: Tenant can update inspection status and findings

metadata.proof: PATCH /api/inspections/{id} depends on current_user (any role), not require_roles. ensure_inspection_scope grants tenants access when tenant_visible=True and unit matches. After the scope check, there is NO role guard — a tenant can modify status, findings, follow_up_tasks, and tenant_visible. This lets tenants alter inspection workflow state and internal notes, which should be staff-only operations.

extra.message: Unbounded CSV import rows cause denial of service

metadata.proof: POST /api/admin/import/{kind} (property_admin only) reads the entire uploaded file into memory (file.read()) then materializes ALL CSV rows into a list (list(csv.DictReader(...))). There is no row-count cap or streaming limit. A crafted CSV with millions of rows causes memory exhaustion (OOM) and unbounded database inserts, enabling denial of service against the server.

extra.message: API keys have no expiration and no revocation path

metadata.proof: The ApiKey model has no expires_at column. The only API key endpoint is POST /api/integrations/api-keys (create). There is no DELETE, PATCH, or listing endpoint to revoke or deactivate keys. While an is_active column exists in the model, the application exposes no way to toggle it through the API. Once issued, API keys remain valid indefinitely unless manually removed from the database, violating the principle of credential lifecycle management.

extra.message: Uploaded documents stored unencrypted at rest

metadata.proof: The Document model stores a filesystem path to uploaded files (lease packets, ticket photos, payment receipts). The save_upload function writes file chunks in plaintext to disk via out.write(chunk) with no encryption. These documents contain PII (names, addresses, financial data from leases) and PHI (ticket photos of living spaces). Anyone with server disk access can read sensitive tenant and property data in cleartext.
